Senses.PreferredTarget: to bring up and call attention to
Senses.Explanation: To bring something up and call attention to it: to prompt a person or repeatedly return a saying or matter to notice and examination. In a public exchange, an unnamed monk asks Gushan Shenyan to prompt him about the lineage matter; Gushan calls him closer and says, "This is prompting you." Hongzhi Zhengjue describes both participants in an exchange as each putting out a hand and bringing up the matter. Dahui Zonggao uses the verb both critically, for going once through an old saying and calling that freedom from words, and instructively, for bringing something up from time to time and amid walking, sitting, emotion, and responsive dealings. Wumen Huikai says many pick up Zhaozhou Congshen's answer and many bring it under examination. Foyan Qingyuan recalls receiving repeated earnest prompting from his late teacher. The Zen bend is the interpersonal and case-facing use: this ordinary act of calling attention becomes something done in the interview, received by Foyan Qingyuan from his late teacher, or repeatedly directed at a recorded saying, without naming a separate regimen.
Senses.Note: The frozen allowlisted corpus has 642 exact hits in 208 files representing 206 works. Eight exact anchors across four works cover request and response as separately attributed turns, case commentary, critical report, occasional prompting, a regional appraisal, memorial thanks, and repeated occasions. Changes of actor, object, and frequency do not create different things, so the entry remains one verb sense.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師却喚近前這個是提撕汝喚作宗乘中事即不得

Occurrences.Kwic: 可謂。一抑一揚。一奪一縱。各出一隻手。提撕此事。且道。是什麼事。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The cited extensive recorded-sayings collection (宏智禪師廣錄): Hongzhi Zhengjue comments that each participant puts out one hand and brings up this matter, then asks what the matter is.

Occurrences.Kwic: 舉時須要以眼顧視。只是以古人言句提撕一遍。喚作不在言句上。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The cited recorded-sayings collection (大慧普覺禪師語錄): Dahui Zonggao critically reports people going once through an old worthy's saying and calling that not resting on words.

Occurrences.Kwic: 也不著忘懷。也不著著意。但自時時提撕。妄念起時。亦不得將心止遏。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The cited recorded-sayings collection (大慧普覺禪師語錄): Dahui Zonggao says not to force forgetting or attention, but simply to bring it up from time to time without suppressing wandering thoughts.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: The cited recorded-sayings collection (無門慧開禪師語錄): Wumen Huikai comments that many throughout the regions pick up Zhaozhou Congshen's answer and not a few bring it under examination.

Occurrences.Kwic: 先師老和尚某奉侍日久多蒙苦口提撕追遠之誠何可忘也
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Sayings of the Ancient Worthies (古尊宿語錄): Foyan Qingyuan says in a memorial address that he served his late teacher for a long time and often received earnest verbal prompting.
